emergency.notes: 112 handles all emergencies. ICE-SAR (Icelandic Association for Search and Rescue): 112. Register your travel plans on safetravel.is before venturing into the highlands or remote areas.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise normal precautions in Iceland. Iceland is one of the safest countries in the world and a popular travel destination. Be aware of natural hazards including volcanic activity.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Most visits to Iceland are trouble-free. Be aware of natural hazards — volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, geothermal areas, and extreme weather. Register your travel plans before going to remote areas.

healthcare.systemType: Universal (Sjúkratryggingar — National Health Insurance) for residents
healthcare.costForTourists: EU/EEA visitors with EHIC receive care at reduced cost. Others pay full price. GP visit ISK 4,000-8,000 ($30-60). Emergency room ISK 10,000-30,000. Iceland has free healthcare for residents but tourists pay full rates. Quality is excellent.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies (Lyfjaverslanir) available in Reykjavik and major towns. Limited in rural areas — bring sufficient supplies. Some English spoken.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Landspítali University Hospital in Reykjavik is the country's main hospital and provides excellent care. Outside Reykjavik, medical facilities are limited. Helicopter air transport is available for emergencies.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance with search and rescue coverage is strongly recommended. ICE-SAR rescue operations are provided free of charge but evacuation costs can be significant. Winter driving requires confidence in 4WD vehicles.

pharmacy.hours: Most pharmacies open 10am-6pm Mon-Fri, shorter hours on weekends; some late-night pharmacies in Reykjavík; on-call pharmacies available 24/7 for emergencies
pharmacy.tips: Many common OTC medications available. Pharmacists are helpful and knowledgeable. Bring all prescription medications you may need — in remote areas pharmacy access is limited. Some medications may require a local prescription.

vaccinations.notes: No required vaccinations for travelers from any country. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date. No special vaccines needed for most travelers. COVID-19 requirements vary — check current entry requirements.

water.notes: Tap water is safe and of excellent quality throughout Iceland. It comes from glacial springs and is among the cleanest water in the world. Bottled water is unnecessary — bring a reusable bottle. Hot spring water from natural geothermal sources is NOT safe to drink.

healthcare.foodSafetyTips: Iceland has very high food safety standards. All food sold commercially is safe. Traditional Icelandic cuisine (lamb, seafood, skyr) from restaurants is safe. Be extremely careful near geothermal areas — some hot springs are toxic if consumed. Do not drink water from hot springs or geothermal pools.

travelInsurance.tips: Healthcare in Iceland is expensive for non-residents. A doctor visit costs $150-300+, hospital stays $1,000+/day. Travel insurance with medical coverage is strongly recommended. Medical evacuation from remote areas (highlands, remote hot springs) can be extremely expensive ($10,000-50,000+). Ensure coverage includes emergency medical evacuation and search and rescue.

healthcare.qualityNotes: Iceland has an excellent healthcare system with highly trained medical professionals. Primary care is available throughout the country. Major hospitals in Reykjavík (Landspítali) and Akureyri. English is widely spoken by medical staff. Pharmacies (apótek) are well-stocked.

medications.prescriptionRules: A valid prescription (ideally from an Icelandic doctor) is required for prescription medications. EEA prescriptions may be recognized for EU/EEA citizens. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's note.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD stimulant medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Stimulants are controlled substances. Bring original prescription, doctor's letter, and only the amount needed. Declare at customs if carrying controlled substances.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is controlled. Some products may be available with prescription. Carry alternatives if possible.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (diazepam, alprazolam, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines require documentation. Carry a doctor's letter explaining medical necessity.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry original prescriptions and a note explaining medical necessity. Given Iceland's remote location, bring more medication than you might think necessary.

connectivity.simOptions: SIM cards from Síminn, Vodafone Iceland, or Nova at the airport and phone shops. EU SIM holders can use EU roaming. Tourist data SIM ~ISK 2,000-5,000 ($15-35) for 5-30GB. eSIM via Airalo.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi widely available in Reykjavik hotels, cafes, restaurants, and many public spaces. N1 gas stations (all over Iceland) have WiFi. Coverage in the highlands and remote areas is very limited.
connectivity.bestOption: EU travelers: use home SIM under EU roaming. Others: Síminn SIM for best nationwide coverage. Buy at Keflavik airport.

cultural.tipping: Not expected or customary. Service charges are included in prices. Leaving a tip is appreciated but never expected. Icelanders do not tip.
cultural.dressCode: Casual and practical. Waterproof jacket and layers are essential year-round. Smart casual in Reykjavik restaurants at night. No strict dress codes.
cultural.greetings: Informal and egalitarian. First names used universally — there are no formal/informal distinctions. Handshake for first meetings. Icelanders can seem reserved at first but are warm once comfortable.
taboos: Disturbing the natural environment — leave no trace strictly
Driving off designated roads and tracks (illegal and damages fragile terrain)
Entering geothermal areas not designated for visitors
Approaching nesting birds (especially Arctic terns — they will attack)
Picking flowers, removing rocks, or taking souvenirs from nature
cultural.haggling: Not practiced. Iceland has fixed, high prices across the board.

safety.lgbtSafety: Excellent. Iceland is one of the most LGBTQ+-inclusive countries in the world. Same-sex marriage legal since 2010. Iceland had the world's first openly gay head of government. Reykjavik Pride is a major celebration.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Very safe. Iceland consistently ranks as one of the world's top countries for gender equality. Women can travel solo with confidence.
safety.notes: Iceland has virtually no crime. The main risks are natural hazards: volcanic eruptions, geothermal activity, sudden blizzards, rivers in flood, and dangerous coastal waves. Never turn your back on the ocean. Register your travel plans on safetravel.is. Weather changes rapidly — always be prepared.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free (Schengen). UK citizens: 90 days in 180-day period. EU/EEA citizens: unlimited.
practical.timeZone: UTC+00:00 (Iceland does not observe daylight saving time)
practical.bestTimeToVisit: June-August for midnight sun, hiking, green landscapes. September-March for northern lights. Winter requires 4WD and experience with icy roads. Highland F-roads open only June-September.

hospitals.name: Landspítali University Hospital
hospitals.notes: Iceland's only university hospital and main acute care facility.

hospitals.name: Akureyri Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital for North Iceland. English-speaking staff.

immediate: Evacuate immediately if within an exclusion zone as declared by Civil Protection
Wear an N95 mask to protect from volcanic ash and sulfur dioxide
Follow police and Civil Protection (Almannavarnir) instructions — do not ignore exclusion zones
Avoid lava fields even if eruption appears calm — lava tube collapses can occur
Close car air vents if driving through ashfall
after: Follow safetravel.is and Almannavarnir for updates on exclusion zone changes
Do not return to evacuated areas until explicitly permitted
Clean volcanic ash from vehicles, gutters, and roofs promptly

immediate: Do not drive in blizzard conditions — roads close frequently in Iceland
Check road.is for current road closures before traveling
If caught in a blizzard while driving, stay with your vehicle
Dress in waterproof, windproof layers at all times when outdoors in winter
after: Check road.is and vegagerdin.is for road status before resuming travel
Allow extra travel time — roads may be icy even after a storm
